content.user_title: Plan a Chrome Accent Color Extension
content.value_statement: Website recoloring requires coordinated color states, CSS overrides, and browser extension controls. This public guide outlines those requirements for an AI-assisted implementation.
actual_capabilities: Outlines a Manifest V3 extension concept using service workers and the Scripting API.
Describes generating hover, active, border, and muted colors from one input color.
Identifies early stylesheet injection and high-specificity selectors as the proposed theming approach.
Lists per-domain settings, local persistence, and custom CSS as intended features.
Describes a vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS workflow without a bundler.
Documents limitations involving framework build steps, shadow DOM, and protected Chrome pages.
limitations: Only SKILL.md is included; extension source, scripts, templates, and assets are absent.
The guide does not provide executable HSL calculations or CSS injection logic.
Production readiness, Manifest V3 compliance, and universal website compatibility are not verified by this package.
The guide excludes React or Vue build workflows and notes restrictions affecting shadow DOM and protected Chrome pages.

prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a vanilla JavaScript Manifest V3 prototype with per-domain toggles and local persistence. Identify required files, permissions, and tests before generating code.

prompt_templates.title: Review implementation risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this extension concept for permission scope, CSS conflicts, shadow DOM limitations, protected pages, and color contrast. Distinguish documented claims from unverified behavior.

best_practices: Treat this package as a planning guide and verify which implementation assets are available before starting development.
Limit extension permissions to approved sites and review generated code before loading it into Chrome.
Test color contrast, site controls, and styling conflicts across representative pages before wider use.
anti_patterns: Assuming the guide includes a deployable extension or the advertised source package.
Claiming universal website support or accessible contrast without testing a real implementation.
Granting broad site access without evaluating whether narrower permissions meet the intended use.

faq.question: Does this package include the extension source?
faq.answer: No. SKILL.md explicitly states that scripts, extension source, and templates from the original package are not included.

faq.question: What browser platform does the guide target?
faq.answer: It describes a Chrome Manifest V3 extension using service workers and the Scripting API.

faq.question: Does the proposed workflow require a bundler?
faq.answer: The guide describes vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS without a bundler. No implementation is included to verify that workflow.

faq.question: Can it recolor every website?
faq.answer: Universal support is not verified. The guide notes restrictions on protected Chrome pages and possible conflicts with shadow DOM elements.

faq.question: Does the guide guarantee accessible contrast?
faq.answer: No. It discusses HSL palettes but provides no contrast measurements or accessibility verification.

faq.question: Can I use this guide with Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use the Markdown guide as context, but extension code must still be implemented or obtained separately.
